workstreams.label: Sourcing
workstreams.owner: Head of origination or a deal partner

workstreams.label: Value creation
workstreams.owner: Head of value creation or an operating partner

activities.label: Screening teasers and CIMs
activities.solution: Read each inbound teaser or CIM, score it against your written mandate, and produce a one-page summary with the reasons to pass or proceed.
activities.first_step: Write your mandate as explicit pass and proceed criteria.
activities.check: A deal professional reviews every pass that scores close to the line.

activities.label: Building market maps and target lists
activities.solution: Build and refresh target lists from licensed databases and public filings, with each company tagged by sub-sector, size indicators, and ownership.
activities.first_step: Choose one sector and compare a generated list with the best list your team has built by hand.
activities.check: An investor confirms each shortlisted name before anyone acts on it.

activities.label: Logging deals and contacts in the CRM
activities.solution: Log deal flow, intermediaries, and meetings in the CRM automatically from the deal inbox and calendar, and flag duplicates.
activities.first_step: Choose one shared deal inbox as a test, and list what is entered by hand today.
activities.check: Sample entries weekly at first, and keep private meetings out of this by rule.

activities.label: Tracking intermediary coverage and follow-ups
activities.solution: Watch CRM and email for contacts going cold, then draft a follow-up with relevant context for the deal owner to approve.
activities.first_step: Agree who counts as a priority intermediary and how long is too long without contact.
activities.check: The relationship owner approves every message. Nothing goes out unreviewed.

activities.label: Reviewing data room documents
activities.solution: Organize the data room, extract key terms and figures with citations to the source page, and flag gaps against your checklist.
activities.first_step: Choose one closed deal as a test, and write down what the team actually found on it.
activities.check: Every extracted fact links to its page, and the deal team verifies anything that reaches a memo.

activities.label: Managing request lists and trackers
activities.solution: Match data room uploads to open requests, update the tracker, and produce a daily list of what is missing and from whom.
activities.first_step: Standardize one request list template across the workstreams on your next deal.
activities.check: The deal lead confirms an item is complete before it closes on the tracker.

activities.label: Summarizing expert and customer calls
activities.solution: Turn call transcripts into structured notes by theme, showing where sources agree and disagree, with quotes to back each point.
activities.first_step: Agree a standard note format, then process the calls from one live or recent deal.
activities.check: Confirm recording consent and expert network rules first, and verify quotes before reuse.

activities.label: Spreading financials into models
activities.solution: Pull figures from management accounts and CIMs into your model template, mapped to your line items, with each number traceable to its source.
activities.first_step: Fix one template and mapping, then test it on three sets of accounts with different formats.
activities.check: An associate ties totals back to source. The model structure and assumptions stay with the team.

activities.label: Drafting IC memos
activities.solution: Produce a first draft in your house format from diligence notes and the model, with each claim linked to its source, so the team edits instead of starting from blank.
activities.first_step: Collect five memos you consider excellent and turn their shared structure into the template.
activities.check: The deal team owns the argument and the recommendation.

activities.label: Finding past deals and precedents
activities.solution: Search past memos, models, and IC notes in plain language, with answers that cite the original document and respect access rights.
activities.first_step: Gather the memos from your last fund, with permissions matching who can see them today.
activities.check: Access rights must carry over, including any information barriers.

activities.label: Assembling packs, minutes, and actions
activities.solution: Assemble the pack from approved versions, circulate it, and track actions until they close.
activities.first_step: Define one folder and naming standard that marks which version is final.
activities.check: The IC chair or secretary approves the minutes, as they form part of the firm's record.

activities.label: The investment decision itself
activities.solution: Keep the decision with the committee. AI can prepare a challenge list of open risks and past comparable deals beforehand.
activities.first_step: Add a short list of counterarguments to the next IC pack and ask members whether it helped.
activities.check: Responsibility for the decision stays with the committee.

activities.label: Comparing NDAs and deal documents
activities.solution: Compare incoming drafts with your standard positions and past deals, and list the deviations for counsel with suggested fallback wording.
activities.first_step: Start with NDAs: write down your standard positions.
activities.check: Counsel reviews all output. This supports the legal review and does not replace it.

activities.label: Running closing checklists
activities.solution: Keep the closing checklist current from email and signature platforms, and chase owners for outstanding items.
activities.first_step: Adopt one checklist format with a named owner for each item on your next closing.
activities.check: Counsel and the deal lead sign off on conditions before they are marked complete.

activities.label: Handing deals over to the portfolio team
activities.solution: Build the post-close record from the memo, model, and final documents: key terms, covenants, reporting duties, and the first plan's owners and dates.
activities.first_step: Define what the portfolio team needs on day one, then build it by hand once from a recent deal.
activities.check: The deal lead and portfolio lead both confirm covenant dates and reporting duties.

activities.label: Negotiating terms
activities.solution: Keep negotiation with your team and counsel. AI can prepare an issues list and show what you accepted on past deals.
activities.first_step: Build a simple record of positions you accepted on recent deals.
activities.check: Keep counterparty and privileged material within approved tools.

activities.label: Chasing portcos for monthly KPI files
activities.solution: Request files on schedule, chase late ones, check they arrived complete, and load them into your portfolio model, with exceptions sent to one owner.
activities.first_step: Agree one KPI template and due date with two portfolio companies.
activities.check: A person handles exceptions and any message that goes to company management beyond a routine reminder.

activities.label: Standardizing KPI data across portcos
activities.solution: Map each company's accounts to your standard definitions with reusable rules, and flag values that break the pattern instead of passing them on.
activities.first_step: Write down definitions for your ten most-used KPIs, and check whether each company uses them the same way.
activities.check: Anyone changing a mapping leaves a record, and reported figures reconcile to company accounts.

activities.label: Writing variance commentary
activities.solution: Draft explanations of movement against budget and prior year from the numbers and management commentary, marking anything unexplained as a question.
activities.first_step: Choose one company as a test, and keep its latest commentary to compare against.
activities.check: The portfolio lead edits and signs off, and causes the data does not support must be marked as unexplained.

activities.label: Spotting underperformance early
activities.solution: Check every new data point against budget, covenant headroom, and trend rules, and send an alert with context to the owner.
activities.first_step: Agree three warning rules with your portfolio leads.
activities.check: Review false alarms monthly, and adjust the rules with the people who receive them.

activities.label: Digesting board packs
activities.solution: Summarize each pack against the last one: what changed, what is missing, and where the numbers and narrative disagree.
activities.first_step: Try it on your last two packs from one company and ask the director what was missed.
activities.check: Directors still read what matters, and board materials stay within approved tools.

activities.label: Preparing questions for the board
activities.solution: Prepare a question list from the pack, open actions, and the investment case, linked to the page behind each question.
activities.first_step: Use it before one board meeting and record which questions the director kept.
activities.check: The director chooses what to raise and how, because these are relationship decisions.

activities.label: Tracking board actions
activities.solution: Extract actions from minutes into one tracker with owners and dates, and bring overdue items into the next pack.
activities.first_step: Move actions from one portfolio company into a shared tracker.
activities.check: The company secretary or director confirms the wording of each action.

activities.label: Board-level judgment and decisions
activities.solution: Keep these decisions with directors. AI can prepare the background.
activities.first_step: List which board decisions recur, and what evidence directors want before them.
activities.check: Directors stay responsible for these decisions.

activities.label: Tracking value creation plans
activities.solution: Keep 100-day and value creation plans current from company updates, link each initiative to its KPI, and draft status reports for owners to confirm.
activities.first_step: Put one company's plan in a shared format, with a measurable KPI on every initiative.
activities.check: Initiative owners confirm status. Status must not be inferred from silence.

activities.label: Reusing what worked across portcos
activities.solution: Make past plans, operating reviews, and results searchable, so a new company can start from what worked in similar situations.
activities.first_step: Write up five past initiatives with their results in a single format.
activities.check: Check for sensitive company data before sharing anything between portfolio companies.

activities.label: Benchmarking portcos
activities.solution: Compare companies with each other and with licensed external data on standardized metrics, and highlight the gaps worth a conversation.
activities.first_step: Pick five comparable metrics and benchmark two similar companies.
activities.check: Confirm definitions match before comparing.

activities.label: Coaching management teams
activities.solution: Keep this with your operating partners. AI can help with their preparation and follow-up notes.
activities.first_step: Ask operating partners which preparation takes the most time before a management session.
activities.check: Management teams should know how any meeting notes are stored and used.

activities.label: Preparing exit data and history
activities.solution: Assemble the performance history, KPI bridges, and vendor diligence inputs from your portfolio data, and flag gaps early.
activities.first_step: Choose one company and list what an exit readiness check should cover.
activities.check: Finance and advisers verify anything that may enter sale documents.

activities.label: Drafting sale materials
activities.solution: Produce first drafts of the equity story and management presentation sections from board packs and plans, with sources marked.
activities.first_step: Draft one section from a past exit and compare it with the final document.
activities.check: Advisers and counsel review all statements before use.

activities.label: Building buyer lists
activities.solution: Build strategic and financial buyer lists with the rationale for each, using recent deals and stated strategies.
activities.first_step: Compare a generated list with the buyer list from a recent process.
activities.check: The deal team and adviser decide who is approached, and handle confidentiality.

activities.label: Deciding exit timing and route
activities.solution: Keep the decision with partners. AI can keep market comparables and readiness data ready for that discussion.
activities.first_step: Define what an exit review for each company should contain.
activities.check: Partners own the decision and the conflicts around it.

activities.label: Drafting quarterly LP letters
activities.solution: Draft fund and portfolio commentary from approved numbers and last quarter's letter, in your house voice, with every figure tied to its source.
activities.first_step: Generate last quarter's letter from last quarter's inputs and have a partner mark up the differences.
activities.check: IR, finance, and a partner approve the letter. Every figure must tie to the books.

activities.label: Filling ILPA and LP-specific templates
activities.solution: Fill ILPA and investor-specific templates from one approved dataset, and run tie-out checks before anyone sees them.
activities.first_step: List every template you produce, and mark where they request the same data.
activities.check: Finance signs off the source dataset, and exceptions are reviewed by a person.

activities.label: Merging data from portcos and the administrator
activities.solution: Combine administrator, portfolio, and valuation data into one quarter-end dataset, reconcile it, and send breaks to named owners.
activities.first_step: Map the data flow for one quarter and note where it is copied by hand.
activities.check: Reconciliation breaks need a person to resolve them, with a record of why.

activities.label: Uploading to portals and distributing
activities.solution: Publish approved documents to the right investor folders with access checks and a delivery record.
activities.first_step: Check that your record of which investor receives which document is correct.
activities.check: Spot-check access lists before each distribution.

activities.label: Answering DDQs and RFPs
activities.solution: Build an approved answer library and draft each new DDQ from it, with citations and a flag on anything stale or unanswered.
activities.first_step: Load your last three completed DDQs and mark which answers remain approved.
activities.check: IR and compliance approve answers, because these are representations to investors.

activities.label: Handling ad hoc LP questions
activities.solution: Classify each incoming question, gather the data and past answers, and draft a reply for IR to review.
activities.first_step: List last quarter's LP questions to find which types recur.
activities.check: IR sends every reply, and compliance checks for selective disclosure.

activities.label: Completing ESG and regulatory surveys
activities.solution: Pre-fill annual ESG and investor surveys from portfolio data and last year's answers, and show what changed.
activities.first_step: Combine last year's surveys and find the overlap between them.
activities.check: The owner checks the evidence and signs off all figures.

activities.label: Sensitive LP conversations
activities.solution: Keep these conversations with partners and IR. AI can prepare a short brief on the investor's history and open points.
activities.first_step: Decide what a good pre-call brief includes for your top ten LPs.
activities.check: Nothing sensitive should be sent without a person deciding.

activities.label: Refreshing pitch decks and PPM sections
activities.solution: Update decks and PPM sections from approved data, and keep figures, case studies, and wording consistent across documents.
activities.first_step: Create a single approved source for your key figures and case studies.
activities.check: Compliance and counsel review all marketing materials under the rules that apply to you.

activities.label: Building track record tables
activities.solution: Generate track record and attribution tables from one audited dataset, with checks that every version ties out.
activities.first_step: Rebuild the current track record from source and record each difference.
activities.check: Finance and compliance verify the method and every published figure.

activities.label: Maintaining the fundraising data room
activities.solution: Keep the data room current by flagging expired documents, mapping LP requests to files, and reporting what each investor has viewed.
activities.first_step: Audit the data room for outdated files and assign each section an owner.
activities.check: IR approves additions, and access controls are reviewed for each investor.

activities.label: Identifying and prioritizing LPs
activities.solution: Rank prospective LPs on mandate fit, past commitments, and relationships, using licensed data and your CRM, with the reasoning shown.
activities.first_step: Test the ranking against the investors who committed to your last fund.
activities.check: IR decides who is approached and follows the marketing rules for each jurisdiction.

activities.label: Keeping LP records in the CRM current
activities.solution: Update LP contacts, commitments, and interaction history from email and calendar, and flag duplicates and departures.
activities.first_step: Clean the top 50 LP records and define what must always be current.
activities.check: Follow your data privacy rules on what is captured, and sample records weekly at first.

activities.label: Writing up LP meetings
activities.solution: Turn meeting notes or approved recordings into a structured summary with next steps, filed against the investor.
activities.first_step: Agree a one-page note format and use it for one month.
activities.check: Get consent for recordings, and the meeting owner approves the note.

activities.label: Tracking investor follow-ups
activities.solution: Track promised follow-ups across email and CRM, remind owners, and draft replies with the right materials attached.
activities.first_step: Start with one list of open commitments from your last ten LP meetings.
activities.check: The owner approves every outbound message.

activities.label: Leading LP meetings
activities.solution: Keep these meetings with partners and IR. AI can prepare a short brief with the investor's history, interests, and open items.
activities.first_step: Prepare a one-page brief for your next five LP meetings and ask whether it helped.
activities.check: Check briefs for accuracy before they are used in the room.

activities.label: Reconciling capital calls and distributions
activities.solution: Match notices, bank movements, and investor allocations automatically, and send only the breaks to a person.
activities.first_step: Measure how many items match automatically on last quarter's calls using simple rules.
activities.check: Payment approvals stay under your existing dual controls, separate from this work.

activities.label: Checking fee and carry calculations
activities.solution: Recalculate fees and carry independently from LPA terms and side letters, and flag differences from administrator figures.
activities.first_step: Write down one fund's fee terms in a form a calculation can follow.
activities.check: Finance reviews all differences before anything changes.

activities.label: Reviewing administrator reports
activities.solution: Check administrator packs against your own records, and list breaks and unusual movements for review before sign-off.
activities.first_step: List the checks your team runs each close and which are always the same.
activities.check: The finance lead signs off, and the review leaves an audit trail.

activities.label: Valuation judgments
activities.solution: Keep the judgment with your valuation committee. AI can compile comparables, prior marks, and policy references.
activities.first_step: Standardize the valuation pack.
activities.check: The committee documents its own rationale for each mark.

activities.label: Tracking side letter and LPA obligations
activities.solution: Extract obligations and restrictions from LPAs and side letters into a register, with dates, owners, and a link to the clause.
activities.first_step: Start the register for one fund, and ask counsel which sample to check.
activities.check: Counsel validates interpretations. The register points to clauses and does not replace them.

activities.label: Preparing regulatory filings
activities.solution: Gather data for recurring filings such as Form ADV, Form PF, or AIFMD reporting, validate it, and show changes since the last filing.
activities.first_step: Map each field of one filing to its data source.
activities.check: Compliance and the responsible officer review and submit every filing.

activities.label: Running attestations and code of ethics checks
activities.solution: Schedule policy attestations, personal trading and gift declarations, chase responses, and keep the record for exams.
activities.first_step: Put all recurring attestations on one calendar with one owner.
activities.check: The CCO reviews exceptions and conflicts.

activities.label: Compliance judgment calls
activities.solution: Keep decisions with your CCO and counsel. AI can surface the relevant policy and past decisions.
activities.first_step: Create a searchable log of past compliance decisions.
activities.check: Your CCO and counsel stay responsible for the decision.

activities.label: Finding documents and past work
activities.solution: Offer plain-language search across shared drives and email archives, with cited answers and existing permissions respected.
activities.first_step: Clean up one high-value folder, then test it with ten real questions from your team.
activities.check: Review permissions first, because search shows people whatever they can already access.

activities.label: Capturing know-how from senior people
activities.solution: Turn recurring partner guidance into playbooks through short interviews and existing documents, then keep them searchable.
activities.first_step: Record one 30-minute interview on the question juniors most often ask.
activities.check: The senior expert reviews each playbook, and it carries an owner and a review date.

activities.label: Onboarding new team members
activities.solution: Give new joiners a guide built from your templates and past work that answers routine questions with sources.
activities.first_step: List the 20 questions that new analysts ask most in their first month.
activities.check: Assign an owner to keep the source material current.

activities.label: Producing internal market research
activities.solution: Produce regular sector briefings from licensed and public sources, with citations and a note on what changed.
activities.first_step: Replace one recurring sector update and ask its readers if it holds up.
activities.check: Show sources to readers, and follow your data licensing terms.

activities.label: Processing expenses and invoices
activities.solution: Read invoices and receipts, code them to the right fund or the management company, and route exceptions for approval.
activities.first_step: Write down your rules for allocating expenses between funds and the management company.
activities.check: Finance reviews fund-versus-manager allocations, and payment approvals stay with people.

activities.label: Coordinating recruiting
activities.solution: Handle interview scheduling and candidate logistics through one process.
activities.first_step: Automate scheduling for one analyst hiring round.
activities.check: People make all assessments and hiring decisions, and employment laws apply.

activities.label: Scheduling and meeting preparation
activities.solution: Prepare meeting briefs from CRM, email, and files, handle routine scheduling, and draft follow-up lists for approval.
activities.first_step: Agree with one partner what a useful daily brief would contain.
activities.check: Assistants or owners approve anything that goes out, and calendar access is controlled.

activities.label: Handling IT and access requests
activities.solution: Handle routine requests and joiner and leaver steps through one request form, with approvals recorded.
activities.first_step: Create a joiner and leaver checklist covering every system.
activities.check: Access changes need named approval and periodic review.
